classification.difficultyReason: Follow the scaffolded sequence of sine-rule angle calculation, triangle angle sum, sine-rule side calculation and area rule, rejecting the supplementary angle using the angle sum.

content.prompt: For a triangle $ABC$, $AC=16.2\text{ cm}$, $AB=18.6\text{ cm}$ and $\angle ACB=60^\circ$. Find, correct to one decimal place:

answer.worked:
By the sine rule,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin\angle ABC}{16.2}&=\frac{\sin60^\circ}{18.6}\\\sin\angle ABC&=\frac{16.2\sin60^\circ}{18.6}\\\angle ABC&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{16.2\sin60^\circ}{18.6}\right)\\\angle ABC&\approx49.0^\circ.\end{align*}$$
The supplementary angle is impossible because it would exceed $180^\circ$ when added to $60^\circ$.

The angles of a triangle add to $180^\circ$. Using the unrounded result from part a,
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAC&=180^\circ-60^\circ-\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{16.2\sin60^\circ}{18.6}\right)\\\angle BAC&\approx71.0^\circ.\end{align*}$$

Using the sine rule and the unrounded angle from part b,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{CB}{\sin\angle BAC}&=\frac{18.6}{\sin60^\circ}\\CB&=\frac{18.6\sin\angle BAC}{\sin60^\circ}\\CB&\approx20.3\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

Using the area rule and the unrounded included angle from part b,
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area}&=\frac12\times16.2\times18.6\times\sin\angle BAC\\\text{Area}&\approx142.5\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$
